title: Gallbladder removal (keyhole surgery)
what: The surgeon removes your gallbladder through 3 or 4 small cuts in your belly. You are fully asleep under general anesthesia.
why: Most often for gallstones that cause pain attacks or inflammation.
duration: surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will say what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you have had belly surgery before
If you or your relatives have had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a checkup with a general doctor. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and your medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you exact times.

prepare.title: What to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, slippers, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: Things for 1 to 3 days in hospital
steps: On the day of surgery, you change into a gown and a cannula is put into a vein
In the operating room, the anesthetist gives you medicine and you fall asleep
The surgeon makes a few small cuts and puts in a camera and instruments
The gallbladder is removed, and the cuts are closed
You wake up in the recovery room, then move to a regular ward
feel: Pain where the cuts are. You will get pain relief
Shoulder pain is common. It comes from the gas used to inflate the belly and passes in 1 to 2 days
after: You can usually get up and walk the same day or the next day
At home, eat gentle food as your doctor advises
Do not lift heavy things for a few weeks
Stitches are removed or dissolve on their own. Your surgeon will tell you
red_flags: A temperature above 38 degrees Celsius, or strong or growing belly pain
Yellowing of the skin or eyes
Redness or pus at the cuts

faq.q: How do I live without a gallbladder?
faq.a: Usually normally. Bile still flows into the gut. At first, the doctor will advise gentle food.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, documents, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
